content: Sarecycline is indicated for the treatment of inflammatory lesions associated with non-nodular moderate-to-severe acne. The recommended dosage is weight-based: for patients weighing less than 54 kg, the dose is 60 mg orally once daily; for those weighing 55–84 kg, the dose is 100 mg orally once daily; and for those weighing 85–136 kg, the dose is 150 mg orally once daily. If no improvement is observed after 12 weeks of treatment, reassessment of the therapeutic approach is advised. The safety and efficacy of sarecycline in patients under 9 years of age have not been established. Co-administration of sarecycline with acitretin is contraindicated due to an increased risk of toxicity, although the exact mechanism is unknown. Similarly, the concurrent use of oral retinoids and tetracyclines, including sarecycline, may elevate the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (benign intracranial hypertension). Sarecycline may reduce the therapeutic effects of amoxicillin, ampicillin, dicloxacillin, nafcillin, oxacillin, penicillin G (aqueous, benzathine, or procaine), penicillin VK, and piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is attributed to the interference of tetracyclines with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitoring for reduced efficacy of penicillins is recommended when used concomitantly with sarecycline. Alternative therapies should be considered. Sarecycline can enhance the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents such as atracurium, cisatracurium, pancuronium, rocuronium, succinylcholine, and vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoidance or the use of alternative drugs is recommended. The co-administration of sarecycline with systemic antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Cholera vaccine administration should be avoided in patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Sarecycline may increase the effects of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates such as abemaciclib, afatinib, aliskiren, ambrisentan, amiodarone, amitriptyline, apixaban, atorvastatin, bendamustine, betrixaban, brentuximab vedotin, budesonide, carfilzomib, carvedilol, ceritinib, cetirizine, and others. This interaction occurs via inhibition of the P-gp efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring for toxicities are advised, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. Multivalent cation-containing products, such as aluminum hydroxide, magnesium carbonate, magnesium trisilicate, calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, calcium/vitamin D, and carbonyl iron, can impair the gastrointestinal absorption of sarecycline, potentially reducing its efficacy. To minimize this interaction, tetracyclines should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Bismuth-containing products, such as bismuth subgallate and bismuth subsalicylate, may also decrease the absorption of sarecycline. Similar dosing separation and monitoring strategies should be employed. Cholestyramine may reduce the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Sarecycline may increase the effects of certain drugs metabolized by P-gp, such as ceritinib, cetirizine, and others, necessitating caution and monitoring for potential toxicities.
